trust_decision.summary: On the client, the OpenSSL/QuicTLS certificate verify callback decides whether the server certificate is accepted. At the pinned commit the built-in path (X509_verify_cert) runs with no host or IP reference identity set, so any CA-trusted certificate is accepted for any server name. The platform verifier is also given SNI=NULL for IP literals, so it skips the name check too.

landing_point.why: The summary names OpenSSL and certificate validation. The client branch of CxPlatTlsInitialize only calls SSL_set_tlsext_host_name and never sets X509_VERIFY_PARAM host/ip, and the verify callback at src/platform/tls_openssl.c:1036 relies on that.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/core/connection.c:1866-1876 (fix inserts the ServerName==NULL -> remote-IP default here, fix.diff:1469-1500). Producer of the name is src/core/connection.c:1968, consumed at src/core/crypto.c:307

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the OpenSSL TLS backend. A NULL server name with a pre-set remote address is a core-layer, address-only connection mode that never sent SNI, so 'there is no name to validate against' sounds like a legitimate opt-out rather than a missing check.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: SNI must still NOT be sent for IP-literal server names, but the IP must still be checked against the certificate's IP SAN. Wildcard certs must keep matching whole labels. The NO_CERTIFICATE_VALIDATION and DEFER_CERTIFICATE_VALIDATION flags must keep accepting, or reporting, instead of failing the handshake. A fix that sends the IP as SNI, rejects IP literals or NULL names outright, or fails hard under deferral breaks legitimate use.

NULL server name with QUIC_PARAM_CONN_REMOTE_ADDRESS set (IPv4 and IPv6)

O7_producer.where: src/core/connection.c:1968 (QuicConnStart stores RemoteServerName, which may be NULL); read at src/core/crypto.c:307 into CXPLAT_TLS_CONFIG; the TLS backend drops IP literals at src/platform/tls_openssl.c:2526

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A pool path that, when Config->ServerAddress is supplied, hands QuicConnStart a NULL or IP-derived name that bypasses the default.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pool already distinguishes a supplied address from a resolved one, and a maintainer could reasonably think the name is redundant once an address is given.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The name check is skipped silently when Host is NULL, and the fix leaves this in place. A planted client caller that passes NULL here, for example on a retry/re-init path, would be a how-type sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The NULL-Host branch legitimately serves server-side client-auth validation, so a client-side NULL looks harmless.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SecPolicyCreateSSL gets a NULL hostname when SNI is NULL. A sibling that keeps passing the old SNI field (NULL for IP literals) instead of ServerName would reopen the route on macOS.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SNI and reference identity were the same field before the fix, so mixing them up is a natural maintainer slip.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second TlsConfig construction, for example a version-negotiation or retry re-init, that omits ServerName.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: TLS contexts get rebuilt across QUIC version changes, and copying only some fields there is plausible.

O9_family: CWE-295 improper certificate validation (missing hostname/IP reference-identity check; null-name fallback to no name check)
